## Historical audit — S0156, visible chunk 1 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/test/commons_163096530/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. No reference or rendered image pixels are visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate editable SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, materials and occlusion. The request prohibited external exploration and reference-image textures. |
| Student response, line 3; execution, line 4 | The student interpreted the scene as multiple bunks, wardrobe, fireplace and room architecture. Its program grouped posts, rails, mattresses and ladders into bunk assets, and used procedural wood/plaster patterns, metal finishes, a camera and lights. These are **modeled objects and intended connections**, not independently verified image content or physical connections. No human pose is described. |
| Execution result, line 5 | Step 1 returned `ok: true`; the runner reports a completed render and saved image and blend file. This establishes technical execution, not visual or geometric correctness. |
| Student audit request, line 8; response, line 10 | Given the reference and step-1 image, the student reported small, low back furniture, an overly wide aisle and pale, flat illumination. It hypothesized camera framing, local bunk placement and material/light causes; proposed a longer lens, lower target, bunk shifts, taller fireplace, darker materials and a smaller repositioned light. These are student visual estimates and diagnoses, not independent verification. |
| Student response, line 14; execution and result, lines 16–17 | The standalone revision implemented those parameter families, including floor-pivot fireplace scaling, and step 2 also returned `ok: true` with a saved render. Its actual visual effect is not visible here. |
| Selection events, lines 18–19 | The runner recorded selection of step 2, then step 1. This excerpt does not establish the ultimate submitted result or why selection changed. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher input, teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is visible in this chunk. The line-10 critique is the student’s own response to a requested visual audit, not teacher feedback. The student independently specified and revised the scene within the supplied workflow; its recorded CLI sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2, 9 and 13). Availability of images to the student does not make their contents available to this audit.

**Outcome and lessons.** Two builds formally rendered successfully; reconstruction quality and final outcome remain **unknown**, not established success, algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption. A transferable procedural lesson from the observed workflow is to separate camera, local geometry and illumination hypotheses and test a revision against a retained fallback. The specific lens, bunk and fireplace changes are task-specific hypotheses, not verified improvements. In particular, part contact, object placement and pose, texture fidelity, camera crop, lighting and any remaining render defects require actual image or geometry inspection. Chunks 2 and 3 are unavailable, so later validation or teacher involvement cannot be inferred.
